A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GG-SSM research. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. All pages were inspected, including v2's added supplementary Section 8; v1 contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original GG-SSM results for eye tracking, time-series forecasting, ImageNet classification, and optical flow in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an MST-algorithm comparison with accuracy and runtime results in Table 8.

M1.justification: The graph weights, Chazelle-based MST construction, and state-propagation equations remain unchanged. Kruskal and Prim appear as ablation alternatives, while the supplement explains the existing component rather than establishing a changed GG-SSM procedure.

E1.justification: The eye-tracking, six forecasting, ImageNet, and optical-flow datasets and tasks are retained, including the optical-flow training datasets. The new ablation reuses ImageNet and ETTh2 without introducing a distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds Kruskal and Prim as evaluated alternatives to Chazelle's MST construction. Comparator membership in Tables 1–7 is unchanged. Boruvka is discussed in the supplement but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The new ablation compares MST algorithms using ImageNet Tiny-scale classification and ETTh2 forecasting at horizon 192, adding relative epoch-time measurements alongside accuracy and MSE. Existing benchmark protocols, training settings, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5 tests whether the MST algorithm affects predictive performance and computational efficiency on two retained tasks. This is a focused component ablation absent from v1, without a broader robustness or sensitivity investigation.

E5.justification: Table 2's uncertainty entries are unchanged, and v2 adds no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The ablation's 'within ±0.1%' describes differences between algorithms, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 are unchanged. Table 8 adds Kruskal/Prim ImageNet accuracies of 83.5%/83.4% and ETTh2 MSEs of 0.356/0.358, plus relative timings. Chazelle's epoch-time ratios are 0.90 and 0.88 relative to Kruskal's 1.00. Its ETTh2 MSE of 0.353 rounds the retained 0.3534 result.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and Section 3.3's complexity argument are retained. Supplementary Section 8 gives an informal overview of the existing MST algorithm and restates its O(Eα(E,V)) bound, without a new formal model, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about dynamic graph construction, efficiency, and broad performance advantages. The headline ImageNet accuracy of 84.9% and KITTI-15 error of 2.77% are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablation as showing similar predictive performance but faster computation with Chazelle, particularly for larger L. Section 8.2 adds discussion of dense O(L²) candidate edges and possible sparse approximations, although it does not resolve the main text's overall O(L) claim.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link advertised for code, poster, and other material. Conversely, removing v1's Figure 2 removes block-level architecture details. Existing hardware, preprocessing, and training hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 69 reference entries are retained. New Section 8 adds limited positioning of Chazelle's algorithm among Kruskal, Prim, and Boruvka alternatives. The rewritten related-work section largely preserves the existing positioning against sequential and predefined-scanning SSMs.

P1.justification: Both related-work subsections are retitled and rewritten. v2 adds an ablation section, a supplementary algorithm overview, and publication/access notices. Most of the introduction, method, experiments, and conclusion retain their wording and narrative order.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from the method section to the first page. The architecture comparison in v1 Figure 2 is removed; v2 Figure 2 is a new MST illustration. Table 8 is added, while existing tables retain their structure and undergo layout relocation.

improvement.justification: The new ablation supplies useful evidence for selecting Chazelle's MST, and the explanatory supplement and code-access link improve accessibility. These gains are limited: Table 8 lacks uncertainty reporting and an input-size scaling study, and the dense-graph versus linear-complexity tension remains unresolved. Removing the architecture diagram also reduces implementation clarity, but the added evidence supports a modest net improvement.
